one_line: Retro iPod-inspired multimedia player with agent proxy control.
what_it_does: Reimagines an iPod Video-era music player in HTML Canvas, with Apple Music/Spotify connectivity and human or agent interaction.
leverage_rationale: The concept benefits from agent-mediated player control, but the visible evidence and description indicate a conventional media-player UI whose outcomes remain broadly achievable through browser automation.
leverage_evidence: Devpost describes direct interaction or agent proxy use.
Screenshot shows only submission packaging, not an agent-controlled player.
execution_rationale: The submission claims a player but provides no product-motion frame sheet and the screenshot does not show the player running, so end-to-end execution is not evidenced.
execution_evidence: No video frame sheets submitted.
Devpost screenshot shows description only and no active player UI.
impact_rationale: A nostalgic, focused music-player experience has a credible audience among music listeners and retro-interface enthusiasts, though the practical value beyond existing players is uncertain.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets interactive multimedia playback and retro nostalgia.
Description names Apple Music and Spotify users.
creativity_rationale: The iPod-era interface revival combined with HTML-in-Canvas and agent proxy interaction is a fresh, memorable synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Explicit iPod Video-era design direction.
Agent-as-proxy framing for a single-purpose player.
usability_note: Potentially focused, but live usability is not shown.
red_flags: Packaging screenshot is not runtime evidence.

one_line: Agent-assisted browser piano lessons tailored to a learner's request.
what_it_does: Turns natural-language requests into visible piano practice sessions with loaded pieces, tempo, hand isolation, loops, count-in, metronome, highlights, and practice mode.
leverage_rationale: The agent and learner share live musical transport and practice state; structured WebMCP changes a chat answer into an immediately configured playable lesson that generic UI driving would reproduce less reliably.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies shared transport, lesson changes, visible key highlights, and activity history.
Claimed workflow includes loading a piece, isolating a hand, looping bars, setting tempo/count-in, and starting practice.
execution_rationale: Frame sheets show a coherent piano/lesson interface with controls, text/instructions, and keyboard states; the stated central workflow is broad and appears intentionally implemented, though audio quality is not assessable.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show browser piano keyboard, controls, settings, and highlighted keys.
Description lists multiple modes and fourteen pieces.
Audio is not assessed per protocol.
impact_rationale: Learners who need adaptive practice receive a concrete, credible improvement over generic advice by having the lesson configured inside the instrument.
impact_evidence: Clear learner problem: advice previously stopped at the chat box.
Visible/playable lesson workflow addresses tempo, hand isolation, looping, and expected-note practice.
creativity_rationale: The interaction model of an agent meeting the learner inside a shared browser piano is notably original and pursued across lesson mechanics.
creativity_evidence: Agent and learner operate on the same piece and transport.
Structured musical arrangements and bar-level practice controls.
usability_note: The interface exposes familiar piano and transport controls while adding agent configuration.
red_flags: Sonic quality and microphone behavior are not assessable from silent frames.
advance_reason: High-quality, well-evidenced use of WebMCP for an adaptive piano lesson.

one_line: Browser-native spreadsheet exposing structured operations to agents.
what_it_does: Provides an in-browser calculation engine and twelve tools for agents to read, write, format, restructure, undo, and point at live workbook state alongside a human.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central: agents operate on live local workbook state with dependency-aware recalculation, returned changed cells, shared focus, and human edits incorporated into replanning.
leverage_evidence: Description explains stable cell addresses, dependency graph, recalculation ripple, and shared human-agent document state.
Frame sheets show chat/workspace progression into an editable spreadsheet artifact.
execution_rationale: Frames show a coherent conversational-to-spreadsheet workflow and populated artifact with toolbar/grid states; the implementation claims align closely with the demonstrated product surface.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show initial chat, processing, and populated spreadsheet artifact.
Description specifies twelve tools and an IronCalc/WebAssembly engine.
impact_rationale: Spreadsheet users and agents have a real precision and reliability problem; keeping computation and editable intermediate state in the workbook directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Specific failure mode: agents transcribe or recalculate spreadsheet state unreliably.
Shared editable workbook and returned recalculation changes provide credible value.
creativity_rationale: The product frames the spreadsheet as the agent's structured workspace rather than asking a model to simulate spreadsheet work, with a distinctive shared-state interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Spreadsheets for models, not models for spreadsheets.
Agent focus color, notes, live edits, and recalculation feedback are integrated into the concept.
usability_note: The familiar grid and toolbar are paired with a conversational workflow; complexity remains plausible for spreadsheet users.
standouts: Strong evidence of artifact completion and shared state.
advance_reason: Transformative agent-native spreadsheet with strong demonstrated execution.

one_line: Source-checked career planning from saved opportunity screenshots.
what_it_does: Converts scattered opportunity clues into official-source-backed, human-approved plans across multiple possible futures, with fit, dependencies, conflicts, and blocked items.
leverage_rationale: The agent must gather structured opportunity facts and stage explainable plans in the same human-editable profile; WebMCP makes multi-future shared planning more reliable than detached answers.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies source verification, staged facts, unresolved items, dependencies, and human approval.
Frames show saved-content transformation into branching plans for Maya.
execution_rationale: The storyboard clearly shows transformation from saved post to populated, branching plans with concrete actions; the full source-checking workflow is claimed but not fully visible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show progressive population of three distinct plan tracks.
Description includes blocked/ineligible and unresolved states.
impact_rationale: People exploring non-linear careers have a real problem of opportunity overload and lost context; source-backed, multi-goal planning directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Specific audience and problem are articulated around saved posts, eligibility, dates, and multiple futures.
Concrete outputs include actions, timing, prerequisites, and evidence goals.
creativity_rationale: The camera-roll-to-source-checked multi-future planning model is an original and memorable career interaction.
creativity_evidence: Three futures branch from one person into different concrete plans.
Saved screenshot is treated as a planning input rather than a bookmark.
usability_note: The plan structure is legible, though source verification and profile setup may be demanding.
red_flags: Specific tool invocation is not directly legible in the silent frame sheets.
standouts: Clear human approval and explainability framing.
advance_reason: Credible, high-impact planning workflow with visible generated plans.

one_line: Adaptive retail workspaces generated from natural-language tasks.
what_it_does: Lets an agent assemble task-ready retail workspaces for clearance, pricing, inventory, and storefront editing while staff review, edit, lock, and approve changes.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP enables the agent to choose trusted blocks and layouts, modify the same workspace, and preserve human review rather than merely describing retail actions in chat.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies 11 trusted React blocks, five layouts, shared service layer, and human approval.
Frames show natural-language clearance request becoming a product collection/workspace.
execution_rationale: Frames show coherent retail dashboard, task request, matched products, and built clearance workspace; the scope is ambitious with only minor unshown edge behavior.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show product analytics, request for 20% off products unsold 90 days, and populated clearance collection.
Description covers responsive layouts and bilingual interfaces.
impact_rationale: Retail staff have a concrete fragmentation and review problem; task-specific workspaces can reduce manual movement across product, inventory, and storefront screens.
impact_evidence: Clearance workflow identifies slow-moving products and exposes prices, stock, photos, and margins.
Human edit/lock/review/approve flow matches operational needs.
creativity_rationale: Dynamically composing trusted interfaces for each retail task is a fresh interaction model beyond a fixed admin dashboard.
creativity_evidence: Four goals and task-specific workspace layouts.
Agent changes the same workspace into a storefront preview.
usability_note: Task-focused workspaces and approval controls appear approachable for retail staff.
red_flags: Long-term persistence and real catalog integration are not independently evidenced.
standouts: Good alignment between natural-language request and visible workspace result.
advance_reason: Clear operational value and demonstrated adaptive workspace workflow.

one_line: Shared planetarium and observing-route planner for people and agents.
what_it_does: Allows a person and agent to query the same live sky, preview and approve routes, set location/time, and advance through observable targets.
leverage_rationale: The product's core state is visual sky context and route planning; structured tools share map, time, location, target, and plan state in a way generic UI driving would be less precise and safe.
leverage_evidence: Description lists ten strict tools reusing manual actions and a read/find/preview/inspect/mutate/save sequence.
Frames show persistent star map, target detail, and route-building states.
execution_rationale: The frames show a coherent planetarium-to-route workflow with map and object detail surfaces; the claimed approval and persistence states are plausible but not all visible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show live sky exploration, selected object details, and manual route building.
Description specifies validation, persistence, and preview that does not mutate state.
impact_rationale: Beginners and hobby astronomers have a real planning burden involving time, place, visibility, and route comfort; the shared planner directly helps them observe.
impact_evidence: Audience/problem is explicitly described as combining observer, time, targets, and comfortable route.
Observable sky and route outputs are central to the product.
creativity_rationale: Treating a planetarium's live visual state as a shared, approval-gated agent workspace is an original application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Preview route without mutating observer state.
Agent proposes a timed route in the same planner rail as the human.
usability_note: Manual exploration and explicit preview/approval support understandable use for beginners.
red_flags: Tool invocation itself is not clearly legible in contact sheets.
standouts: Excellent safety sequence for shared state.
advance_reason: Strong shared-state WebMCP concept with credible visual execution.

one_line: Human-approved shift handoff accountability for multi-location cafes.
what_it_does: Turns closing notes into owned, deadline-bound risks and proposed handoffs; agents can read and propose but humans alone can approve verification.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP creates a constrained shared workflow where the agent can inspect live risks and propose plans but cannot perform the critical approval action, making the safety boundary concrete.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies eight tools, six read-only, and no agent tool for marking verification.
Frames show closing-handoff task, ownership, editing, and progress states.
execution_rationale: The frames show a coherent handoff record moving from incomplete/unowned to assigned and reviewable; the described audit behavior strengthens completeness.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show closing handoff, task details, assignment/ownership, and progress states.
Description reports testing an attempted unauthorized approval and checking the audit log.
impact_rationale: Shift risks such as cash discrepancies, refrigeration, and stock have real operational and safety consequences; ownership and deadlines directly address the missing-hour problem.
impact_evidence: Specific cafe/multi-location audience and concrete risks.
Handoff requires owner, deadline, and backup plan before safe status.
creativity_rationale: The explicit capability boundary—agent proposes but cannot approve—is a thoughtful interaction and safety model applied to shift operations.
creativity_evidence: No tool can mark a handoff verified.
Shared handoff accountability rather than generic note summarization.
usability_note: The workflow is operationally legible, with visible assignment and review states.
red_flags: Live agent invocation is not directly identifiable in frames.
advance_reason: High-impact workflow with meaningful constrained agent collaboration.

one_line: Preview-only social feed gate where humans choose what to reveal.
what_it_does: Lets agents inspect compact previews, explain them, and propose a queue while the person independently selects and reveals full stories.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes a constrained preview/proposal surface rather than full content, enabling agent assistance without surrendering the human reveal decision; the contract changes the interaction model materially.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies four narrow tools and no full post content.
Frames show preview gate, proposed strategy, persistent preview panel, and human-choice messaging.
execution_rationale: Frames present a coherent preview-to-choice flow and persistent explanatory UI; the demo scope is deliberately narrow and appears complete for it.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show preview-first states, selected reveal strategy, and persistent gate context.
Description specifies filtering, queue proposal, and ordinary reveal action.
impact_rationale: People overwhelmed by feeds have a credible desire for explainable attention planning and control over disclosure, though the demo's value is narrower than a full feed product.
impact_evidence: Clear human-control problem: prevent an agent silently deciding what to open.
Preview metadata and independent selection address blind opening.
creativity_rationale: The preview packet and human-selected reveal gate are a novel, memorable interaction model for agent-mediated social content.
creativity_evidence: Agent proposes and explains; person selects and reveals.
Explicitly avoids exposing full post content to the agent-facing surface.
usability_note: The preview/reveal distinction is clear and supported by persistent explanatory copy.
red_flags: Privacy is described as a demo coordination contract, not server-enforced privacy.
advance_reason: Original and coherent human-controlled attention workflow.

one_line: Private pantry, recipe, and shopping assistant with local WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Tracks pantry inventory, recipes, allergies, shopping, expiration, and planning locally, exposing tools for grounded agent queries and recipe workflows.
leverage_rationale: The agent can query and reason over live private pantry state, recipe gaps, expiration, and appliance timing without data leaving the device; this is more than UI button automation.
leverage_evidence: Description claims thirteen tools for pantry summaries, expiring items, recipe gaps, substitutions, rankings, and timing.
Frames show dashboard metrics, recipe/planning screens, privacy settings, and assisted page interaction.
execution_rationale: Frames show a substantial dashboard and multiple workflow surfaces including inventory, recipe/planning, privacy, and completed assisted interaction; the exact agent call sequence is not fully legible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show inventory status, counts, recipe/planning, privacy/data ownership, and output states.
Description specifies localStorage, no backend, and a broad tool surface.
impact_rationale: Households have a concrete pantry visibility and meal-planning problem; privacy-first grounded assistance can reduce waste and answer practical questions.
impact_evidence: Specific pantry discovery problem motivates the product.
Features cover expiring food, missing ingredients, shopping, allergies, and appliance constraints.
creativity_rationale: A privacy-first local pantry becoming an agent-readable household knowledge base is a fresh angle on a familiar inventory app.
creativity_evidence: Local-only design is tied directly to WebMCP access.
Tools support multi-recipe timing and expiration rescue planning.
usability_note: Dashboard metrics and privacy controls provide a clear household workflow, though feature breadth may increase complexity.
red_flags: Some external-page interaction details are difficult to distinguish from browser tooling in frames.
advance_reason: Credible local agent-assisted pantry workflow with visible product breadth.

one_line: Shared invoice-reconciliation dashboard with agent pointing and draft chasers.
what_it_does: Reconciles messy cross-border payments, lets agents query receivables and highlight exact rows in the human view, and drafts reviewable chaser letters.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP connects structured reconciliation reasoning to the exact dashboard row and reviewable draft, improving shared reference and reducing disconnected agent explanations.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies eight tools, embedded structured data, tab switching, row flashing, and draft chaser letters.
Frames show dashboard, agent/action panel, and side-by-side interaction states.
execution_rationale: Frames show a coherent dashboard with KPIs/table and agent-assisted action panel; the stated reconciliation and drafting workflow is substantial, though some transitions are presentation overlays.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show dashboard table, highlighted/demo states, and tool/action drawer.
Description names tolerance for fees, batched and split payments and review-only sending.
impact_rationale: Cross-border invoice reconciliation is a concrete high-friction finance task for businesses; matching deposits and drafting follow-up directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Specific agri-export use case with wrong amounts, fees, and poor references.
Product surfaces unpaid invoices, payment behavior, explanations, and chaser drafts.
creativity_rationale: The shared row-pointing and reviewable chaser workflow is a thoughtful application of WebMCP, though invoice dashboards are an established category.
creativity_evidence: Agent can flash the exact row in the human's own view.
Nothing is sent automatically; human review is built in.
usability_note: Dashboard plus explicit agent panel and reviewable draft fit finance operations, though dense data may require onboarding.
red_flags: Some frame captions/overlays are demo presentation rather than direct state evidence.
advance_reason: High practical value and clear shared human-agent dashboard workflow.
